blocks.text: Why Photoshop remains essential for social media

Many tools exist for quick social media graphics. Yet, Photoshop remains the choice for professional creators. It offers precision that web based tools often lack. You can manage complex layers, handle high resolution files, and use advanced masking techniques. This is vital when you produce content for multiple platforms with different aspect ratios.
Setting up your Mac for Photoshop performance

Photoshop is resource intensive. Ensure your Mac meets the requirements. You need at least 16 GB of RAM for smooth performance with multiple artboards. Use an SSD with at least 4 GB of free space for your scratch disk. If you notice lag, check your preferences under Photoshop > Settings > Performance. Adjust the memory usage to allow Photoshop to use more RAM. This keeps your interface responsive during long editing sessions.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for your workflow

items: Cmd + Shift + N to create a new layer.
V to select the Move tool.
Cmd + Z to undo your last action.
Cmd + Plus or Minus to zoom in and out.

blocks.text: Memorizing these shortcuts changes how you interact with the canvas. You stop hunting through menus and keep your eyes on the design. If you forget a shortcut, ask Lazur to point it out. Hold Option + Command and ask where to find a specific tool. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item for you.

One common mistake is editing pixels directly. Always use adjustment layers and layer masks. This allows you to change your mind later. If you want to remove a background, use a mask instead of the Eraser tool. This keeps your original image intact. If you need help with a mask, ask Lazur to explain the steps for creating one.
How to manage your time as a creator

You spend a lot of time on administrative tasks. Communication and planning consume over half your day. Use tools like Notion for your content calendar. Keep your Photoshop files organized in clearly named folders. Use standard naming conventions like YYYYMMDD_ProjectName_Version. This saves you from searching for files later.

items: Working in the wrong color mode. Always check Image > Mode to ensure you are in RGB for web content.
Ignoring resolution. Set your canvas to 72 or 300 PPI depending on the final output.
Not saving often. Enable auto save in your preferences.
Overcomplicating layer structures. Use groups to keep your panel clean.

Next steps for your design process

Start by auditing your current workflow. Identify which parts take the most time. Is it resizing images? Or maybe creating templates? Focus on automating those specific tasks. Use Actions in Photoshop to record repetitive steps. Once you have your actions, use Lazur to help you remember how to trigger them. Consistency will improve both your speed and the quality of your social media presence.
